guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not treating Kansas’ 51-6 opener as proof that it will consistently create that kind of separation. We saw an impressive performance: Kansas gained 613 yards, held Long Island to 146 and got 246 passing yards plus 49 rushing yards from new starting quarterback Isaiah Marshall. The more important question for us is how much to carry forward against a stronger opponent.

Our numbers show Middle Tennessee’s clearest path through its passing game and its ability to create scoring opportunities against a Kansas defense that grades less favorably in those areas. That case is balanced by Kansas’ defensive pressure—the Jayhawks recorded 11 tackles for loss in the opener—and by the uncertainty surrounding an offense that lost nine starters from 2025. For us, the positives and concerns largely offset each other, leaving our view closely aligned with the market and without enough value to justify a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Middle Tennessee’s passing offense against the Kansas pass defense. Our numbers suggest this is where Middle Tennessee has the best chance to sustain drives, but Kansas brings meaningful experience on the back end: Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander combined for 22 starts last season, while Taylor Davis started 10 games. If Kansas pairs that secondary experience with the disruption it showed in the opener, Middle Tennessee’s most plausible route to staying competitive becomes much narrower.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, the eighth-highest single-game yardage total in program history.
Kansas rushed for 277 yards and five touchdowns against Long Island.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and six points.
The Kansas defense recorded 11 tackles for loss and kept Long Island out of the end zone.

opponent_notes.fact: Kansas is scheduled to host Middle Tennessee on Oct. 3, 2026 at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium; the game time was listed as TBA.

quarterback.fact: Head coach Lance Leipold named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall Kansas' starting quarterback before the 2026 season.
Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Marshall's start against Long Island was his second career start after appearing in a dual-quarterback starting role against Kansas State in 2025.
Backup Cole Ballard entered 2026 with 15 career appearances and one start and had completed 35 of 64 passes for 445 yards and three touchdowns.

Quarterback Chase Jenkins transferred from Rice after starting all 12 regular-season games there in 2025, when he passed for 1,025 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 531 yards and five touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back Yasin Willis, a transfer from Syracuse, rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns in his Kansas debut against Long Island.
Running backs Dylan Edwards and Jalen Dupree also made their Kansas debuts against Long Island; Edwards had six carries for 32 yards, while Dupree had nine carries for 35 yards and a touchdown.
Wide receiver Nik McMillan, a transfer from Buffalo, caught six passes for 130 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas debut.
McMillan entered the next game with seven consecutive 100-yard receiving performances dating to his 2025 season at Buffalo.
Nahzae Cox transferred to Kansas from upcoming opponent Middle Tennessee and recorded a 47-yard reception in his Kansas debut against Long Island.
Kansas returned two 2025 starters on the offensive line: left tackle Calvin Clements and left guard Amir Herring, both of whom started all 12 games in 2025.
The Game 2 depth chart listed Kasen Carpenter at center, Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard and Nick Morrow at right tackle alongside Clements and Herring.
Carpenter transferred after starting two games for Oklahoma State in 2025 and 11 games for Tulsa in 2024; Morrow transferred after starting five games for California in 2025.
Kansas lost nine offensive starters from 2025, including quarterback Jalon Daniels, running back Daniel Hishaw Jr., center Bryce Foster, guard Kobe Baynes and tackle Enrique Cruz Jr.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island after leading Kansas with 4.5 sacks in 2025.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery against Long Island.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returned after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Kansas returned cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts in 2025, and safety Taylor Davis, who started 10 games in 2025.

The secondary added experienced transfers Corey Gordon, Jaden Harris and Roman Pearson; Gordon started 12 games for Louisville in 2025, Harris had 13 starts for Miami in 2024 and Pearson started eight games for Ball State in 2025.
Kansas returned five defensive starters from 2025: Lathan, Alexander, Davis, defensive tackle Blake Herold and Todd.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after two seasons at Penn State; he previously coordinated Kansas' offense from 2021 through 2023.
D.K. McDonald remained Kansas' defensive coordinator, and Daryl Agpalsa remained the offensive line coach.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett did not play in Kansas' season opener against Long Island; the notes did not state a reason.

Boston College transfer linebacker Bam Crouch started four games in 2025 before missing the remainder of that season because of injury; Kansas listed him as a starting linebacker or co-starter on its Game 2 depth chart.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas had six plays of at least 20 yards and three plays of at least 40 yards against Long Island.
Kansas did not allow a sack and surrendered only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
Kansas had allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest total in the Big 12 over that span.
Kansas averaged 19.7 yards per completion over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, the highest figure in the Big 12 over that span.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, ranking fourth in the Big 12.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, long snapper Rino Monteforte from California and freshman punter Matt Gill for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart listed Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas entered the Missouri game 1-0 overall and was scheduled to face Arizona State in London before hosting Middle Tennessee.
Kansas listed 32 transfer additions for 2026: 13 on offense, 17 on defense and two on special teams.
